keys.error.cancelled: Nothing was changed. Your old recovery key still works.
keys.error.pinned_floor_downgrade: The new key would have lowered a limit this device keeps for the account. Nothing was sent, and nothing was changed.
keys.error.pinned_kek_generation: The server shows an older recovery key than this device has seen. This can be an attack, or the server was restored from a backup. Nothing was changed. If the server was restored and you accepted the older state on this device, use “Reapply the unlock methods” on this page. If not, tell whoever runs the server.
keys.error.reapply_not_offered: Reapplying the unlock methods is offered only after an older state of the server was accepted on this device, and only for that restore. Nothing was changed.
keys.error.renew_pin_save_failed: The server took the new recovery key, but this device could not save its record of the change. The new key works, and the old one no longer does.
keys.error.renew_unconfirmed: The server's answer did not arrive in a form this page can trust, so the new key may or may not be in force. Keep both the new and the old page 2. Make a new recovery key again when the server answers; that one replaces both.
keys.error.sheet_server_key_missing: This device's record of the account does not hold the server's key, so page 1 cannot be made here. Sign out, sign in again and try once more.
keys.error.sk_not_remembered: This device does not remember the secret key, so page 1 cannot be made here. The secret key is on page 1 of the sheet you have.
keys.reapply.done: The recovery key is back on the server, as a new key above the one the restore brought back.
keys.reapply.from_restored_note: The unlock methods went back with this restore. You can put a new recovery key in place now, while the vault is open.
keys.reapply.heading: Unlock methods after a restore
keys.reapply.intro: You accepted an older state of the server on this device ({date}). The server holds older unlock methods than this device has seen.
keys.reapply.nothing: There was nothing to reapply: the server's recovery key is not older than the one this device has seen. Nothing was changed.
keys.reapply.password: The master password on the server is the older one too, and this device will refuse it at the next unlock. Change your master password while the vault is open to put a new one in place.
keys.reapply.recovery: Reapplying makes a new recovery key and puts it on the server above both the restored key and the one this device has seen. The key from the backup stops working on this server.
keys.recovery.busy_saving: Saving the new key on the server.
keys.recovery.cancel: Do not use the new key
keys.recovery.done_backup: The server was asked to make a new backup.
keys.recovery.done_heading: The new recovery key is in force
keys.recovery.done_keep_old: If the server is restored from a backup from before this change, the old key works again and the new one does not. Keep the old sheet until you have seen a new backup.
keys.recovery.done_old_key: The old recovery key no longer opens the vault on this server. Your devices stay signed in, and page 1 of your sheet does not change.
keys.recovery.effects: Once the server has the new key, the old key no longer opens the vault on this server. Page 1 of the sheet and your secret key stay the same, and your devices stay signed in.
keys.recovery.heading: New recovery key
keys.recovery.intro: A new recovery key replaces the one on page 2 of your emergency sheet. You are asked for your master password first. The new key is then shown once: write it down or print it, and type it back. Nothing changes on the server before that.
keys.recovery.title: Recovery key
keys.secret.heading: Your secret key
keys.secret.intro: The secret key is on page 1 of your emergency sheet. A new browser or device needs it together with your master password. Type it in there, or read it from the QR code shown here. You are asked for your master password first.
keys.secret.no_secret_key: This account has no secret key.
keys.secret.not_remembered: This device does not remember the secret key, so it cannot be shown here. You find it on page 1 of your emergency sheet.
keys.secret.qr_alt: QR code with the secret key
keys.secret.title: Secret key
keys.secret.warning: Whoever sees the key or its QR code and also knows your master password can sign in to your vault. Show it only where nobody can look on.
keys.sheet.download_warning: The file holds your secret key. Do not save it in a folder that is synced or backed up to the cloud (OneDrive, iCloud Drive, Dropbox, Google Drive and the like). Save it to a removable drive or print it, and delete the copy afterwards.
keys.sheet.failed: Page 1 could not be made. Nothing was saved.
keys.sheet.heading: Emergency sheet again
keys.sheet.intro: Page 1 can be made again on this device: the address, your e-mail, the account id, the secret key and the setup QR code. You are asked for your master password first.
keys.sheet.not_remembered: This device does not remember the secret key, so page 1 cannot be made here. Keep the page 1 you have, or make it again on a device that remembers the key.
keys.sheet.page_two: Page 2, the recovery key, cannot be shown again: no device keeps it. For a new page 2, make a new recovery key.
keys.sheet.title: Emergency sheet
